record.prompt: Our API gateway runs 4 worker processes (deploy/server.conf) and limits each API key to 100 requests a minute in gateway/limits.py. Read https://docs.quillon.example/config and tell me whether a key really gets 100 per minute overall, or more.
record.final_answer:
A key can get **more than 100 a minute, up to 400.**

**Why:**
- `gateway/limits.py` creates `Limiter(rate="100/minute", key="api_key")` without a `backend` argument. Nothing else in the repo sets one, so it uses the default `memory` backend.
- The Quillon 1.8 docs say that with `memory`, "each process counts on its own, so an application with N worker processes lets a key make up to N times the configured rate." `requirements.txt` pins `quillon==1.8.2`, so that page applies.
- `deploy/server.conf` sets `workers = 4`, so each worker gives a key 100 a minute, or **up to 400 a minute** overall. How many a client actually gets depends on how its requests are spread across the workers. If they all land on one worker, it gets close to 100.

**It gets worse at the minute boundary.** The docs say windows are "fixed and aligned to the clock," so every counter resets at the start of each minute. A client can use its full allowance at 12:00:59 and again at 12:01:00. That means **up to 800 requests in about two seconds**, while still never going over 400 in any single calendar minute.

**Fix:** To make 100 a minute hold across all workers, switch to the shared backend:

```python
limiter = Limiter(rate="100/minute", key="api_key", backend="tally", url="tally://host:7070")
```

This needs a running tallyd server. The burst at the minute boundary will still happen, because the docs describe only fixed windows. I haven't changed anything; tell me if you want me to make this edit.
